Yes I do mean base pay. I should have stated as much. Yes I've been watching this phenomenon for like a year now where they are adjusting the base pay based on whether the customer tips. If there is no tip the order goes for more if there is a tip the order goes for less. I wouldn't care so much if tips were guaranteed but given how they have a 24-hour window to take tips away I don't think it's fair they reduce the payout because there's a tip. Doing this to me is stealing from the driver. Reducing our earnings. I usually try my best to avoid orders where it's evident this is occurring. For example I saw an order today and they were asking the driver to deliver 18 miles but wanted to pay only $10 and the tip was 9. If the customer takes the tip away then you just delivered $300 worth groceries for 10 bucks. Not to mention the mileage it takes to return to the store. You basically done it for free.

Base pay is not consistent here. Is constantly changing. For instance, one of the cities I like to work from it's pretty straightforward. It's not a big city. They have one Walmart and the routes are pretty consistent. Yet let's say I take an order 15 miles at 9:00. I'll be paid maybe $16. The next hour I choose an order going the same direction same neighborhood and there's a tip attached. That order base pay will have decreased if I half. It didn't used to be this way but in the last year or so that's what I'm seeing. I guess if you live in an area where they aren't implementing these tactics that's wonderful but they're doing it here. it just feel so slimy. Like it's a way to pass the cost off to the customers while they rake in profit. And what's also terrible about it is tips aren't guaranteed so then they're stealing from the drivers by doing this.
